transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, well, I came in because I just feel wound up almost all day. It's... it's like my body is constantly bracing for something. Even when I’m just sitting at my computer working, or trying to relax after dinner, I just can't seem to shake that feeling.
How long have you been feeling this wound up?
It's been going on for a little over a year now... about thirteen months, I'd say. It started right around the time my sister down in Arecibo began needing a lot more help from the family.
Besides concerns about your sister, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several other areas of your life?

Yes, I really do. Um, my mind just keeps going from one concern to another. It's not just my sister. I'll start worrying about whether I missed something at the office, or... or my husband driving home, my church commitments, the bills. It's just a constant stream. I constantly find myself preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet.
Since this began, have you often felt down or hopeless?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I haven't felt hopeless or... or particularly down. It's really just the worrying and the tension. My mood itself is mostly fine, I just can't seem to turn my brain off.
When you try to stop or redirect your worrying, how difficult is it for you to control it?

It's very hard to control. I try, I really do. I'll tell myself, Daniela, enough, focus on this report. But... one small thought just turns into five more. Before I know it, I've spent half an hour checking messages or replaying everything that could go wrong.
Do you often experience muscle tension, such as tightness or soreness in your shoulders, neck, or jaw?
No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My neck and shoulders feel fine, and my jaw doesn't ache or anything. It's really just the constant thoughts, not so much physical pain or tightness.
Does your worrying continue even on days when there are no new problems or urgent concerns involving your sister?

Yes, it really does. Even if there's no new information about my sister in Arecibo, my mind just... it keeps going from one concern to another. If it's not her, I'm worrying about whether I missed something at the office, or I'm stressing over my husband driving home. Then I'll start thinking about my church commitments, or the bills. I just constantly find myself preparing for problems that haven't even happened yet, no matter how quiet the day is supposed to be.
Has your worrying caused you trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Well, most nights I do fall asleep eventually. But staying asleep is harder. I tend to wake up around three or four in the morning, and right away my mind is going over my sister’s next appointment, or maybe some server issue at work. And the frustrating part is, even when I manage to get enough hours, I just... I start the morning feeling like I never really rested at all.
